extraction_rules_applied.numbers: verbatim only; nothing rounded, converted, normalized or supplied from outside knowledge
extraction_rules_applied.equations: rasterized GIFs recorded by filename, never reconstructed

cutoff_model.architecture: Per-zone, per-report multi-criterion flag model. Zones x Reports x Input curves. Each report evaluates its own independent cut-off set per zone and emits its own flag curve; cumulative thickness curves are integrated from the flags.

report_count.value: up to 5 Summation Reports (2 fixed: Reservoir, Pay; + 3 optional)
report_count.verbatim: You also have the option to set up and execute up to 5 Summation Reports . This allows you to generate 3 extra sets of output, in addition to the traditional Net Reservoir and Net Pay Summation reports.

input_curve_count.verbatim: Up to 10 input curves can be entered into this screen for use in the summation computation. The first three curves are pre-defined as 1. Porosity , 2. Water Saturation , and 3. Clay Volume . The additional 7 curves (rows 4 - 10) are clearly defined options and can be any selected input curve. For example, a calculated permeability curve might be used.

cutoffs.name: Phi Cut Res/Pay
cutoffs.verbatim: If the input porosity curve value is greater than or equal to this value, then the level can be considered for Pay or Reservoir if the level also meets all the other cut-offs.

cutoffs.name: Sw Cut Res/Pay
cutoffs.verbatim: If the input water saturation curve is less than or equal to this value, then the level can be considered for pay or reservoir if the level also meets all the other cut-offs.

cutoffs.name: Vcl Cut Res/Pay
cutoffs.verbatim: If the input clay volume curve is less than or equal to this value, then the level can be considered for pay or reservoir if the level also meets all the other cut-offs.

cutoffs.name: Other cut-off 1
cutoffs.verbatim: Other input curve 1 cut-off value. If you decide to apply some cut-off criteria, and if the other input curve 1 is >= or <= (depending on setting on input curve window) to this value, then the level can be used in the report if the level also meets all the other cut-offs.

cutoffs.name: Other cut-off 2
cutoffs.verbatim: Extra input curve 2 cut-off value. If the extra input curve 2 is >= or <= (depending on setting on input curve window) to this value, then the level can be considered for pay or reservoir if the level also meets all the other cut-offs.

cutoffs.name: Other cut-off 3
cutoffs.verbatim: Extra input curve 3 cut-off value. If the extra input curve 3 is >= or <= (depending on setting on input curve window) to this value, then the level can be considered for pay or reservoir if the level also meets all the other cut-offs.

cutoffs.name: Min Res Height
cutoffs.verbatim: Allows you to set the minimum thickness of a zone in order for it to count as net reservoir. Default is 0. (All depth intervals will count towards net if they meet the cut-off criteria).

cutoffs.name: Min Pay Height
cutoffs.verbatim: Allows you to set the minimum thickness of a zone in order for it to count as Net Pay. Default is 0. (All depth intervals will count towards pay if they meet the cut-off criteria).

cutoffs.name: Min XXXX Height (optional reports)
cutoffs.sense: minimum-thickness gate on the optional report
cutoffs.verbatim: Allows you to set the minimum thickness of a zone in order for it to count in whatever Report computation is being executed. Default is 0. (All depth intervals will be counted, if they meet any cut-off criteria that may have been set).

cutoffs.name: Minimum Height (multi-well)
cutoffs.verbatim: The Minimum Height allows you to set the minimum thickness of a zone in order for it to count as net reservoir ( Reservoir sub-tab) or net pay ( Pay sub-tab). The default is 0. (All depth intervals will count towards net if they meet the cut-off criteria).

gross_net_pay_layering.gross: Zone top to zone bottom (Gross Interval, non-editable result parameter). Zones may have gaps between them.
gross_net_pay_layering.net_reservoir: Levels passing the Reservoir report cut-offs. Conventionally: 'The Reservoir Results tab allows you to view the results of a summation calculation for Net Reservoir - determined by the application of the Porosity and optional Clay Volume cut-off criteria - for each defined zone.'
gross_net_pay_layering.net_pay: Levels passing the Pay report cut-offs. Conventionally: 'The Pay Results tab allows you to view the results of a summation calculations for Net Pay - determined by the application of the Vclay, Porosity and Water Saturation cut-off criteria - for each defined zone.'
gross_net_pay_layering.coupling: NOT enforced as a hierarchy. Pay is a separate report with its own independent cut-off column. The only stated coupling is a UI convenience: 'Values typed into the Reservoir report column for Porosity, Water Saturation and Clay Volume automatically populate the appropriate cells in the Pay report column.'

curve_type_preprocessing.verbatim: Phi - clip the input curve to values greater than zero.

Vcl - clip the input curve to values between zero and one. This allows you, for example, to select a clay volume from GR curve as the input. IP will clip the curve values to lie between zero and one before the summation calculations are performed.
Sw - clip the input curve to values between zero and one. Also, this Type initiates a computation of a porosity-weighted average for the input curve when computing zonal averages.

averaging_methods.verbatim: The Average Method column allows you to define the averaging method to apply to input curves. The options are available from a drop-down list. The options are : Arithmetic , Geometric and Harmonic .
averaging_methods.guard_rule: For the Geometric and Harmonic averages, any input value which is less than or equal to zero, will be ignored and not included in the final average.
averaging_methods.zonal_basis: On the main report all zone averages are thickness weighted averages not arithmetic averages.

depth_integration_convention.verbatim: Each depth in the data is considered a discrete interval, with the recorded depth being the center of the interval. Therefore, when making averages over an interval, only half of the top and bottom depth increments are counted.
depth_integration_convention.interval_thickness_rule: The net thickness is determined by Bottom minus Top plus depth step. The Top is the depth of the first instance of where the flag curve turns on. The Bottom is last depth where the flag curve is on. To illustrate this further; think of an interval where there is just one step with the flag curve on. Top = Bottom but thickness will be the depth step.

multiwell_rollup_arithmetic.verbatim: In Multi-Well mode an average property is computed by adding together the value thickness of the parameter for all selected wells, then by dividing the result by the total thickness in all wells.
multiwell_rollup_arithmetic.worked_example_verbatim: Well 1 (Zone 1) Av Phi 0.195 / Net Thickness 50ft / Phi H 50 x 0.195 = 9.75 / Av Sw 0.25 / Phi So H 9.75 x (1-0.25) = 7.313 ; Well 2 (Zone 1) Av Phi 0.165 / Net Thickness 20ft / Phi H 20 x 0.165 = 3.3 / Av Sw 0.30 / Phi So H 3.3 x (1-0.3) = 2.31 ; Combined: Phi H 9.75 + 3.3 = 13.05 / Net Thickness 50 + 20 = 70ft / Phi So H 7.313 + 2.31 = 9.623 / Av Phi 13.05 / 70 = 0.187 / Av Sw 1.0 - 9.623 / 13.05 = 0.263
multiwell_rollup_arithmetic.definitions_verbatim: Phi = Porosity ; Sw = Water Saturation ; So = Hydrocarbon saturation = 1 - Sw ; Phi So H = Net Hydrocarbon Pore thickness ; Phi H = Net Porosity thickness
multiwell_rollup_arithmetic.note: Av Sw is back-computed from the PhiSoH/PhiH ratio, not averaged directly. This is the only textual (non-rasterized) statement of the porosity-weighted-Sw rule in the manual.
multiwell_rollup_arithmetic.field_average_rule: The field averages are net thickness weighted averages. (multi_wellcutoffsandsummati.htm)

horizontal_well_handling.verbatim: If a TVD summation report is made of a near horizontal well, where the well actually reverses direction and goes upwards, then the module reports the actual vertical thicknesses cut by the well. The zonal averages calculated are weighted by the vertical thickness for each depth increment, so in a nearly horizontal well the zonal TVD averages could be considerably different to MD averages.
horizontal_well_handling.marker_verbatim: The summation report adds a ?*? in front of all net and gross TVD thicknesses where the well is rising with measured depth. This is to inform the user that the results might not be as initially expected.
horizontal_well_handling.worked_figures_verbatim: TVD top is -6077.38 and bottom is -6136.13 which gives a depth difference of 58.75?. However the report gives a gross TVD thickness of *79.5?

cutoff_model.equation_symbol_legend_verbatim: i = ith input value ; h i = ith input interval ; n = number of samples

example_cutoff_values_NOT_defaults.warning: These are the manual's worked EXAMPLE screen values, explicitly not stated as shipped defaults. Do NOT adopt as IP defaults.
example_cutoff_values_NOT_defaults.verbatim: Reservoir (default) - Porosity >= 0.1, Clay Volume ,<= 0.5 | Pay (default) - Porosity >= 0.1, Clay Volume <= 0.5, Water Saturation <= 0.5 | Sw < 0.45 (optional) - Porosity >=0.1, Clay Volume <= 0.5, Water Saturation <= 0.45 | PHIT > 0.15 (optional) - Clay Volume <= 0.5, Water Saturation <= 0.5, Porosity (note different porosity curve selected) >=0.15
example_cutoff_values_NOT_defaults.printed_listing_verbatim: Phi Pay > 0.100 ; Sw Pay < 0.500 ; Vcl Pay < 0.500 (against curves PHIE / SW / VWCL)

cutoff_sensitivity.what_it_varies: exactly one cut-off parameter at a time, swept Start -> Stop by Step
cutoff_sensitivity.varies_verbatim: Select the Cutoff parameter to investigate. This could be any of the Cutoff parameters saved by the Cutoff and Summation module, but normally will be Phie, Sw or Vcl.
cutoff_sensitivity.sweep_spec_verbatim: Enter the Cutoff Start Value , Cutoff Stop Value and the Cutoff Step for the selected Cutoff parameter. These numbers are the minimum and maximum limits for the selected Cutoff parameter and the step is the amount to increment the selected parameter between these two limits.
cutoff_sensitivity.example_sweep_verbatim_NOT_default: In the example below, the PHI cutoff limits to test are from 0.0 to 35 pu, using a 1.0 pu increment.
cutoff_sensitivity.engine_verbatim: The module cycles through the Cutoff parameter limits from Start to Stop value, using the Step, running the Cutoff and Summation module in each selected well.
cutoff_sensitivity.reports: any Summation output parameter, multiple simultaneously, per named Zone or 'All Zones'
cutoff_sensitivity.output_parameter_classes_verbatim: 1. Average properties e.g Av Vcl Res, Av Phie Res or Av Sw Pay & 2. Value Thickness products e.g. PhiH Res (Net Porosity Thickness Reservoir), PhiSoH Pay (Net Hydrocarbon Pore Thickness Pay)
cutoff_sensitivity.percentile_default_verbatim: IP defaults to display the 10th, 50th and 90th Percentile results. These include the Cutoff value corresponding to that Percentile and the Value of the selected output parameter for that percentile.
cutoff_sensitivity.bidirectional_grid_verbatim: You can type in a new Value , Percentile or Cutoff into the appropriate cell, Key Enter or click elsewhere on the grid and IP will recalculate the other two values and update the graphic display.
cutoff_sensitivity.motivation_verbatim: Deciding what values of Vclay, Porosity and Sw to use as Cutoffs is quite often guesswork and therefore sensitivities run on the Cutoff values can be useful in helping to make a decision on the appropriate Cutoff value to apply.
cutoff_sensitivity.save_locations_verbatim: When run on a single well the Save Results operation will save a results file into the active wells sub-folder in the active IP database. | When run in Multi-Well mode the Save Results operation will save the results file to the IP project folder level.

monte_carlo.model_verbatim: The Monte Carlo Error Analysis Module uses a Monte Carlo simulation to estimate the errors in a petrophysical analysis. You enter the distribution of possible errors associated with the interpretation parameters and the input curves. IP, using the error distributions, randomizes the input parameters and makes multiple passes through the analysis modules. The results for each simulation are accumulated and a distribution of the results can be made.
monte_carlo.modules_in_workflow_verbatim: Clay Volume, Porosity SW, Mineral Solver, Basic Log Analysis , NMR , Cutoff, Formula, Multi-Line Formula, Fuzzy Logic, Neural Networks, Multi-Linear Regression, Cluster Analysis, Curve from Zones, Interp_Demo.
monte_carlo.cutoff_coupling_verbatim: The Cutoff module is not required in the work flow list, but when not used, it limits the results to only showing the foot by foot errors on the output curves.

distributions.name: Gaussian
distributions.parameters_taken: Low Value Shift and High Value Shift about the Initial Value, plus the Type Shift algebra
distributions.width_mapping_verbatim: For the Gaussian distribution the Low Value Shift + High Value Shift represents four standard deviations.
distributions.truncation_verbatim: The Gaussian distribution is limited to 2.5 standard deviations either side of the Mean value. If the random number generator comes up with a value outside of this range, then another random number will be chosen.
distributions.truncation_rationale_verbatim: This is done to try and keep the distribution within reasonable limits, since very large shifts in parameters will make some parameters, like Rw, have non-sensible results (negative) and will result in the interpretation module refusing to run.

distributions.name: Triangular (listed as 'Triangle' on the Mineral Solver and Input Curves tabs)
distributions.parameters_taken: Low Value Shift and High Value Shift about the Initial Value
distributions.shape_parameterisation: not stated in manual (mode/peak location never given; the shape diagrams are images)

distributions.name: Square
distributions.parameters_taken: Low Value Shift and High Value Shift about the Initial Value

shift_types.name: Linear
shift_types.verbatim: The parameter is changed by adding or subtracting the shift. Result = Input + Shift

shift_types.name: Percent
shift_types.verbatim: The parameter is changed by using a percent shift. Result = Input x (1 + Shift / 100)

shift_types.name: Reciprocal
shift_types.verbatim: The reciprocal of the parameter is changed by adding or subtracting the shift. Result = 1 / ( 1 / Input + Shift )

seed_handling.verbatim: IP uses a random number generator, seeded through the CPU clock time, to calculate the shifts for each parameter for each simulation. At the start of each simulation, each parameter is changed using a different random number.
seed_handling.user_settable_seed: not stated in manual - no seed control offered; runs are therefore not reproducible in IP2018

correlation_handling.range_verbatim: A Correlation parameter of zero (0) will mean that there is no correlation. A value of 1 equates to a 100% correlation and a value of -1 equals an inverse 100% correlation.
correlation_handling.mechanism_verbatim: The Correlation works by taking the randomly-selected shift for Parameter 1 and applying the same shift to dependent Parameter 2 . If the correlation is negative then the shift will be the inverse amount. For correlation coefficients of less than 1, the correlated shift will then have a randomness applied to it - depending on the value of correlation. A coefficient of 0.5 will apply a randomness of half what would have been selected if the coefficient was 0.0.
correlation_handling.worked_example_values_verbatim: an m and n dependency correlation of 0.5 and a Neu Wet Clay and Rho Wet Clay dependency correlation of -0.8
correlation_handling.scheme_note: Pairwise directional shift-copy, NOT a covariance/Cholesky scheme. Consistency of a joint correlation matrix over 3+ parameters is not stated in manual.

monte_carlo.percentile_convention: By default, the 10 th percentile will be the 10 th percent lowest value of all the simulation results, except for Sw where it will be the 10 th percent highest value. If this convention is not required, then it can be modified by editing the MonteCarloDefaults.par file (stored in the IP directory) and changing the Results section at the end of the file. [source_page: define_monte_carlo_parameters.htm] -- reinforced for output curves on the same page: 'The program sorts for each depth level all the results and then calculates the percentile value. P5 will be the 5th percentile lowest value. P50 will be the middle value.' READING: ascending/statistical convention (Pn = n-th percent LOWEST) for every parameter EXCEPT Sw, which is FLIPPED to n-th percent HIGHEST so that P10 is the optimistic case for both volumes and saturations simultaneously. The flip is a configurable convention stored in MonteCarloDefaults.par, so two installations can disagree - any imported Sw percentile must carry its convention. Interpolation method (nearest-rank vs linear) is not stated in manual.
monte_carlo.percentile_independence_caveat_verbatim: At the end of the MonteCarlo simulation run, which could involve several thousand iterations, the values used for every parameter are ranked from low to high and basic statistics are run on each one. The Mean and Percentile results are calculated on an individual parameter-by-parameter basis. So, for example, the AvPhi Res P50 value will not necessarily come from the same simulation iteration as the Av VCL Res parameter P50 value. This means that a straight multiplication of the P50 Gross thickness, P50 Net to Gross Ratio, P50 AvPhi Res and P50 (1- Av Sw Res ) values will not yield the exact P50 value for the Net Pay Thickness Res ( Phi * So * H ) parameter, though it should be close.
monte_carlo.output_curve_mnemonics_verbatim: XXX MN Mean Result curve | XXX PSD Plus one standard deviation | XXX MSD Minus one standard deviation | Where XXX is the original curve name

tornado_plot.method_verbatim: For each parameter in the Monte Carlo analysis, two runs are made; one with the parameter set to its low value and one set to its high value (± 2 standard deviations for Gaussian distributions). All other parameters are kept to their default values.
tornado_plot.note: Sampler truncates Gaussians at +/-2.5 sigma but tornado endpoints are taken at +/-2 sigma. Both figures stated on the same page; no reconciliation given.
tornado_plot.annotation_verbatim: A % sign indicates that the shift for the parameter is in percent. An R character indicates that this is a reciprocal shift
tornado_plot.ordering_verbatim: The plot is displayed with all selected input parameters shown in the Y axis with decreasing importance towards the bottom of the plot.
tornado_plot.invalidation_verbatim: Any change in the Monte Carlo Error Analysis set-up will mean the Tornado Plot error runs will have to be re-made.

defaults.context: No shipped default iteration count is given anywhere in the module documentation.
The auto stop will always run a minimum of 200 iterations and then check for a stop case every 100 iterations after this.
then check for a stop case every 100 iterations after this.
Hence the minimum number of iterations is 300.

The simulation stops when the difference between the last check and the current check, ie what is the difference change in the parameter value during the last 100 iterations, is less that the entered value (default 0.1%).

defaults.value: the hydrocarbon pore volume in the reservoir zone
defaults.context: You can select the ?Result Parameter? to check for convergence between iterations. The default is the hydrocarbon pore volume in the reservoir zone.
The user selects which zone to check for convergence in (?Result Zone?), default is the ?All? zones average value.
The program checks for difference in the P10, P50, P90 and mean values and makes sure they are all within the tolerance specified and only then will stop the simulation.
If this box is cleared then just the mean value and the standard deviation error curves are saved. Default is to save all results.
All parameters by default are selected. Many of these parameters will in fact not be used in the analysis.

defaults.value: Mineral end-point value plus or minus 10% of the valid value
defaults.context: Low / High Values - default values are filled in which are equal to the Mineral end-point value plus or minus 10% of the valid value. These default values can be modified. (Same wording repeated on the Input Curves tab.)
The Output Curve Names allows you to select up to 10 curves to be output.
Up to nine different histograms can be displayed together.
Up to nine different crossplots can be displayed together.
The Overlay box allows you to select what type of overlay lines are displayed on the histogram. The default is to have a Gaussian distribution.

defaults.setting: Normalize Histogram Maximum Height to 1.0 - Log low value
defaults.context: When turned on the ?Log low value? is set to -1 and the ?Log high value? to 1.

defaults.context: When turned on the ?Log low value? is set to -1 and the ?Log high value? to 1.
Click here to view an example of the Auto Log Plot with the default input curves. The original curves ( PHIE , SW, VWCL and PHIT ) are displayed as dashed lines.
The defaults are saved to the MonteCarloDefaults.par , file stored in the IP directory. Also: 'The default crossplots and histograms can be changed by editing the MonteCarloDefaults.par file'.

defaults_verbatim.context: The Result Precision column allows you to type in / define the number of decimal places to which the zonal average values are reported in the file or print output. The default setting is 3 decimal places.
The maximum setting is 6 places of decimal.

defaults_verbatim.context: However, the text string length to file or printer is set to 8 characters, so setting to a Result Precision of 6 is only useful for reporting very small decimal numbers, for example very low, small fractional permeabilities.

defaults_verbatim.context: Report titles permit a maximum 25 alphanumeric characters in each text box.

defaults_verbatim.context: The Short Name allows a maximum of 4 characters in the name.
The Report Title row allows you to type in names that will be used to distinguish each Summation calculation in an output report. The defaults are Reservoir and Pay reports.

Min Pay Height: Allows you to set the minimum thickness of a zone in order for it to count as Net Pay. Default is 0.

defaults_verbatim.setting: Cut-off & Summation - default report file extension
defaults_verbatim.context: The Normal Report -> File option launches a Save Parameters to File dialog where the results will be written to a specified file name in the default output directory . The default file name uses the name, with the " .txt " extension.

defaults_verbatim.setting: Cut-off & Summation - comma delimited output extension
defaults_verbatim.context: The Comma Delimited option will write the file using commas to separate the fields and will have a file extension of " .csv ". This facilitates loading the data into a spreadsheet application.

defaults_verbatim.setting: Cut-off & Summation - tab delimited output extension

validation_rules.rule: Net cannot exceed Gross
validation_rules.status: NOT STATED IN MANUAL - implicit only. All N/G values in the worked listings are <= 1.000 but the constraint is never written.

validation_rules.rule: Flag curves must be produced
validation_rules.verbatim: The PayFlag and ResFlag curves are used in the interactive log plot display, and should always be calculated.

validation_rules.rule: Flag curves must be produced (multi-well, stronger wording)
validation_rules.verbatim: The Pay Flag and Reservoir Flag curves must be output. However, their names can be changed from the default names.

validation_rules.rule: Porosity and Sw are mandatory inputs; Vcl is conditional
validation_rules.verbatim: One must set up the Porosity and Water Saturation curves to be used for the report. A Clay Volume curve is optional. ... The Clay Volume curve is optional, but must be entered if clay volume is used as a cut-off.

validation_rules.rule: Sub Total zones carry no cut-offs
validation_rules.verbatim: Sub Total zones are not displayed on the interactive plot and have no associated cut-offs, but use the interpretation results from the normal zones to determine net pay or net reservoir average properties.

validation_rules.rule: Sub Totals excluded from the multi-well cut-off grid
validation_rules.verbatim: All zones, set up in the Zones tab, will be displayed here except Sub Totals . Sub Totals have no associated cut-off values, since they are created from other zones, which have their own cut-offs defined .

validation_rules.rule: Cumulative curves are zone-scoped
validation_rules.verbatim: The output cumulative curves are calculated after each zonal computation. They include only the data within all the defined zones. Therefore, if a level is not defined as being in a zone, it will not be included in the cumulative curves, regardless of whether the level meets the cut-off criteria.

validation_rules.rule: Geometric/Harmonic averages reject non-positive values
validation_rules.verbatim: For the Geometric and Harmonic averages, any input value which is less than or equal to zero, will be ignored and not included in the final average.

validation_rules.rule: Post-Run edit lock on the setup tab
validation_rules.verbatim: after the first time that the Run button is pressed, any changes to the cut-off parameter values must be made on the Cut-off and Summation Parameters screens or on the interactive log plot. ... once the Run button has been used, the default settings for cut-off values can no longer be edited on the second set-up tab.

validation_rules.rule: Re-calculation is explicit, not automatic
validation_rules.verbatim: NOTE: Simply changing a parameter in the display will not immediately mean that a zone is re-calculated . You must click the OK button again in order to re-calculate all zones and update all displays.

validation_rules.rule: Zone locking blocks all parameter edits in that zone
validation_rules.verbatim: The Lock Zone column enables youto lock zones. This prevents any changes being made to the parameters in that zone in any of the tabs within the module. It also prevents changes being made interactively to the zones in the Cut-off and Summation Interactive plot.

validation_rules.rule: Gaps between zones are legal
validation_rules.verbatim: It is possible to have gaps between zones. To remove a gap, drag the bottom of the zone above a gap to below the top of the zone below the gap.

validation_rules.rule: Absent zones encoded as blank top/bottom
validation_rules.verbatim: Zones do not have to exist in all wells. Blank zone Top and Bottom depth cells indicate that a zone is absent in a well.

validation_rules.rule: Zone X/Y in report requires a deviation survey and surface location
validation_rules.verbatim: These coordinates can only be computed if the well has a valid deviation survey and surface location loaded into IP.

validation_rules.rule: Monte Carlo shift values must be positive
validation_rules.verbatim: The Low Value Shift and High Value Shift columns set the ranges for the shifts in the parameters. These values must be positive values .

validation_rules.rule: Monte Carlo Gaussian truncation with resampling
validation_rules.verbatim: The Gaussian distribution is limited to 2.5 standard deviations either side of the Mean value. If the random number generator comes up with a value outside of this range, then another random number will be chosen.

validation_rules.rule: Monte Carlo prerequisite - modules must have been run first
validation_rules.verbatim: NOTE: In order for any modules to be used in the work flow, they must have been set up and run on the well data before using the Monte Carlo module. You must, therefore, have made an interpretation before starting . This includes the User Programs .

validation_rules.rule: Formula-module constants cannot be perturbed directly
validation_rules.verbatim: If you want to use a constant value in an equation and vary that constant during the simulation; then the constant value must be converted into a Constant curve (using the formula module) and use the curve, instead of the constant value, in the original formula.

validation_rules.rule: Formula modules skip the depth-range overlap check
validation_rules.verbatim: The User Formula and Multi-Line Formula modules, if they are included in the simulation run, do not verify the depth ranges overlap, but just run the interval specified on the formula input.

validation_rules.rule: Monte Carlo run errors from out-of-range parameters
validation_rules.verbatim: These are caused when the input parameter has been adjusted by IP to have a value that lies outside the normal expected range, and the interpretation module will not run with that value. ... The parameters that are most likely to cause this problem are resistivity-type parameters, which make no sense if they become negative.

validation_rules.rule: Cutoff Sensitivity prerequisite
validation_rules.verbatim: As a prerequisite to using these modules the ? Cutoff and Summation ? module or the Multi-Well Cutoff and Summation module must initially have been run on all wells that are to be run in the sensitivity computation.

validation_rules.rule: Multi-well sensitivity requires identical curve names and a common zone set
validation_rules.verbatim: Multi-Well mode requires that input curves (typically the Porosity, Clay volume and Water saturation curves) in all the wells have the same names. In addition, when using multiple wells, a common Zone set should exist. Note that not all zones have to be present in every well. The module identifies if a zone is missing from a well and warns you, before continuing to process other wells.

validation_rules.rule: Batch Monte Carlo requires a saved Model file
validation_rules.verbatim: Before the Batch Monte Carlo can be run, a parameter model file must be created in the regular Monte Carlo Uncertainty Analysis module. This is done by setting up and running the Monte Carlo Error Analysis module on one well.

validation_rules.rule: Batch Monte Carlo per-well output directories must differ
validation_rules.verbatim: This file will be put into each wells output directory. Therefore, it is important that separate output directories are used for each well, otherwise the results will all be written to the same file.

validation_rules.rule: Batch Monte Carlo missing-curve tolerance
validation_rules.verbatim: If a curve is missing for a well then an Error Dialog will be displayed informing you that an Input Curve is missing and to Continue anyway with the Batch Run. You can choose to ignore the error and continue. If this is done then this curve will be removed from the Monte Carlo input curves. [outputs:] You can continue but no statistics will be generated for the missing output curve.

validation_rules.rule: Multi-well cut-off overwrites single-well module state
validation_rules.verbatim: Once this module is run, all the settings and results produced will also be found populating the single well module . Therefore, if one does not want to lose the settings and results that are currently in the single well cut-offs they should be saved before starting to use the Multi Well cut-off module.

validation_rules.rule: Multi-well cut-off setup is not persisted on exit
validation_rules.verbatim: The Multi Well cut-off setup is not saved when you exit IP or change the database . Therefore, it is good practice to save the format after running the module.

validation_rules.rule: File Loader attribute names must be unique
validation_rules.verbatim: Attribute names must be unique entries.

validation_rules.rule: Fixed attributes cannot be deleted
validation_rules.verbatim: Log Attribute Names prefixed with a double asterisk ( ** ) are fixed attributes and cannot be deleted from the reference table.

validation_rules.rule: Reduced well folder structures are not retro-applied
validation_rules.verbatim: If the user removes folders from the Well Folder Structure then it is only newly created Wells that will have the reduced Well Folder Structure . ... This is to prevent users from inadvertently deleting data that may reside in the removed folders.

validation_rules.rule: Percentile results are per-parameter, not iteration-consistent
validation_rules.verbatim: The Mean and Percentile results are calculated on an individual parameter-by-parameter basis. So, for example, the AvPhi Res P50 value will not necessarily come from the same simulation iteration as the Av VCL Res parameter P50 value.

gaps: MonteCarloDefaults.par contents are never shown. The manual names the file and its parameter indices (3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 for cut-off inputs; also referenced from clayparameters.htm and swparameters.htm for Clay Volume and Phi/Sw inputs) but lists no default shift value, no per-parameter default distribution, and no syntax for the Results section that controls the percentile convention.
No shipped default numeric cut-off values anywhere. The 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.5 and > 0.100 / < 0.500 / < 0.500 figures are explicitly the manual's worked EXAMPLE screens. Do not adopt as IP defaults.
No default Monte Carlo iteration count. Only the auto-stop floor (200 burn-in / 100 check interval / 300 minimum total) and a batch-page prose recommendation of 2000.

The six summation equations are rasterized GIFs (embim160.gif - embim165.gif) and are not recoverable. The multi-well roll-up worked example on cut_off_sensitivity_results.htm is the only textual statement of the averaging arithmetic.

Triangular and Square distribution parameterisation beyond the Low/High shift pair - no mode position, no truncation rule. Only Gaussian has a full spec (Low+High = 4 sigma span, +/-2.5 sigma truncation, resample on reject).
Percentile interpolation method (nearest-rank vs linear vs Hazen) is not stated.
No user-settable random seed. 'seeded through the CPU clock time' means IP2018 Monte Carlo runs are not reproducible.
+/-2.5 sigma (Monte Carlo sampler truncation) vs +/-2 sigma (Tornado plot endpoints) are both stated on define_monte_carlo_parameters.htm with no reconciliation.
'Net cannot exceed Gross' is never asserted as a constraint anywhere in the cut-off documentation.
The 'Interactive Line Sensitivity' pixel default value is not stated.
The Cut-off Type drop-down's actual option strings (presumably '>=' / '<=') are never listed verbatim; the manual only describes it as 'the sign of the cut-off type'.

Internal filename inconsistencies in default_settings.htm: UserCurveType.opt vs UserCurveTypes.opt; UnitConversion.par vs UnitsConversion.par. Also Overlay_Files.ovl (default_settings.htm, tools.htm) vs Overlay_Files.ovlx (intro_file_formats.htm lists BOTH as 'Overlay List File'). Probe for both spellings if ever reading IP config.
Correlation beyond pairwise: no statement of how three or more mutually-dependent parameters are reconciled, nor whether the resulting joint correlation matrix is guaranteed positive-definite.
.cos and .cosr file schemas are named but never specified.
The layout of MonteCarloDefaults.par implied by the 3/6/9/12/15/18 index spacing (three slots per cut-off) is inferred, not stated.

No Tier-B primary literature citations appear on any of the seven target pages: the cut-off/summation model, the sensitivity module and the Monte Carlo module are all described without reference to published sources.
